stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{6}{\sqrt{x}}\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(6\sqrt{x}\), which multiplies by \(\sqrt{x}\) instead of dividing by it; the exponent must be negative.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of treating \(\sqrt{x}\) as \(x^{2}\); the square root is \(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of rationalizing the denominator but squaring it: \(\frac{6}{\sqrt{x}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}} = \frac{6\sqrt{x}}{x}\), not \(\frac{6\sqrt{x}}{x^{2}}\).

verify:
X0 = Symbol('x'); x = symbols('x', positive=True)
v = lambda k: value(choices[k]).subs([(X0, x)])
t = 6/sqrt(x)
assert simplify(v(answer) - t) == 0
assert all(simplify(v(k) - t) != 0 for k in choices if k != answer)
